title: Vanishing higher direct images: cohomology of the direct image equals cohomology upstairs
statement: Let $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a morphism of sites given by the continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), with $f_*=u^s$, $f^{-1}=u_s$, unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^{-1}$ and counit $\varepsilon:f^{-1}f_*\to\mathrm{id}$ of $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ on abelian sheaves. For $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ let $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ ($q\ge0$) be the right derived functors of the left exact functor $f_*:\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive], computed from an injective resolution of $\mathcal F$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal D)$ and, for $p\ge0$, let the edge map $e^p_{V,\mathcal F}:H^p(V,f_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(u(V),\mathcal F)$ be the composite of the pullback $f^*:H^p(V,f_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(u(V),f^{-1}f_*\mathcal F)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] with $H^p(u(V),\varepsilon_{\mathcal F})$ ($H^p$ over an object as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2)). If $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$ for all $q>0$, then $e^p_{V,\mathcal F}$ is an isomorphism for every $p\ge0$. (In degree $0$ it is the identity of $(f_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(u(V))$, by the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}(u(V))\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal F}(V)=\mathrm{id}$.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0733 (lemma-apply-Leray, line 2347), part (1), via the Leray spectral sequence Lemma Tag 0732 (lemma-Leray, line 2323); direct images of injectives: Lemma Tag 072Z (lemma-direct-image-injective-sheaf)

proof.text: *Setting; $f_*$ is left exact additive.* Write $s:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ for an injective resolution of $\mathcal F$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ with $\mathcal I^q=0$ for $q<0$; it exists because $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is abelian with enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1). By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), $f_*=u^s$ is precomposition with $u$: $(f_*\mathcal G)(W)=\mathcal G(u(W))$ and $(f_*\psi)_W=\psi_{u(W)}$ for $W\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal D)$. Hence $f_*$ is additive (addition of morphisms is sectionwise), and it preserves kernels: kernels in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ are sectionwise kernels [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (1), so $(f_*\ker\psi)(W)=\ker(\psi_{u(W)})=\ker((f_*\psi)_W)$. So $f_*$ is left exact additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive] and, for every $W$, $\Gamma(W,f_*\mathcal G)=\Gamma(u(W),\mathcal G)$ and $\Gamma(W,f_*\psi)=\Gamma(u(W),\psi)$ as groups and maps; in particular $\Gamma(V,f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal I^\bullet)$ as complexes of abelian groups.

source.place: Section 01FT (cohomology over an object) and Lemma Tag 0733 (lemma-apply-Leray, line 2347)

proof.text: *$f_*$ of the injective resolution is an injective resolution of $f_*\mathcal F$.* (a) Each $f_*\mathcal I^q$ is injective in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$: $f_*$ is right adjoint to $f^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), and $f^{-1}:\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)\to\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is an exact additive functor of abelian categories [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], so [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] applies (Stacks Homology, Lemma Tag 015Z; for sites Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 0730 with $\mathcal O=\mathbf Z$, and Lemma Tag 072Z, which gives the weaker total acyclicity for ringed topoi). (b) Exactness: by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] applied to $v=f_*$ and the resolution $s$, there are isomorphisms $\iota^q:R^qf_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$; by hypothesis $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$ for $q>0$, so $f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ is exact at $f_*\mathcal I^q$ for every $q\ge1$. In degree $0$, by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (2) for the left exact additive $f_*$ (step 1), $f_*(s)$ induces an isomorphism $f_*\mathcal F\to\ker(f_*d^0)$; so $f_*(s)$ is a monomorphism with image $\ker(f_*d^0)$. Hence $0\to f_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{f_*(s)}f_*\mathcal I^0\to f_*\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$ is exact, and $f_*(s):f_*\mathcal F\to f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] with $f_*\mathcal I^q=0$ for $q<0$.

proof.text: *The pullback computed from this resolution.* Let $r:f^{-1}f_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ be an injective resolution in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ with $\mathcal J^q=0$ for $q<0$ ([lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1)). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] to $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal F$ with the injective resolution $f_*(s):f_*\mathcal F\to f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ of step 2 and the resolution $r$: there is a morphism of complexes $\beta:f^{-1}f_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ with $\beta^0\circ f^{-1}(f_*s)=r$, and by its clause (1) (independence of the choices) $f^*:H^p(V,f_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(u(V),f^{-1}f_*\mathcal F)$ is $f^*=(\iota^p_{\mathcal J})^{-1}\circ H^p(c)\circ\iota^p_{f_*\mathcal I}$ with $c=\Gamma(u(V),\beta)\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^\bullet}(V):\Gamma(V,f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(u(V),f^{-1}f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J^\bullet)$, where $\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^\bullet}$ is the unit applied termwise and $\iota^p_P$ are the identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] for $v=\Gamma(V,-)$, resp. $\Gamma(u(V),-)$ (the identifications $H^p(W,\mathcal G)=H^p(\Gamma(W,P^\bullet))$ of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2)).

proof.text: *The map induced by the counit.* By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists] (for $h=\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}:f^{-1}f_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ and the injective resolutions $r$ and $s$) there is a morphism of complexes $\psi:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ with $\psi^0\circ r=s\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] for $v=\Gamma(u(V),-)$, $H^p(u(V),\varepsilon_{\mathcal F})=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(u(V),\psi))\circ\iota^p_{\mathcal J}$. With step 3, $e^p_{V,\mathcal F}=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}\circ H^p\bigl(\Gamma(u(V),\psi\beta)\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^\bullet}(V)\bigr)\circ\iota^p_{f_*\mathcal I}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0733 (lemma-apply-Leray, line 2347), part (1); the direct proof its proof calls 'a good exercise'

proof.text: *$\psi\beta$ is homotopic to the counit of the complex.* Let $\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^\bullet}:f^{-1}f_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ be the counit applied termwise; it is a morphism of complexes by naturality of $\varepsilon$ at the differentials. Let $\alpha:(f^{-1}f_*\mathcal F)[0]\to f^{-1}f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ be the morphism given by $f^{-1}(f_*s)$ in degree $0$. Since $f^{-1}$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], it carries the exact sequence $0\to f_*\mathcal F\to f_*\mathcal I^0\to f_*\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$ of step 2 to an exact sequence, so $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism. In degree $0$, $\psi^0\beta^0f^{-1}(f_*s)=\psi^0r=s\,\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}$ (steps 3, 4) and $\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^0}\circ f^{-1}f_*(s)=s\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}$ (naturality of $\varepsilon$ at $s:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^0$); all other degrees of $(f^{-1}f_*\mathcal F)[0]$ are $0$. So $(\psi\beta)\circ\alpha=\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^\bullet}\circ\alpha$, and since $\mathcal I^\bullet$ is bounded below with injective terms, [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] gives a homotopy $\psi\beta\simeq\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^\bullet}$, $\psi^n\beta^n-\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^n}=d k^n+k^{n+1}d$. Applying the additive functor $\Gamma(u(V),-)$ gives a homotopy $\Gamma(u(V),\psi\beta)\simeq\Gamma(u(V),\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^\bullet})$, and composing with the chain map $\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^\bullet}(V)$, $H^p(\Gamma(u(V),\psi\beta)\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^\bullet}(V))=H^p(\Gamma(u(V),\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^\bullet})\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^\bullet}(V))$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0733 (lemma-apply-Leray, line 2347), part (1); the direct proof its proof calls 'a good exercise'

proof.text: *Triangle identity; conclusion.* For each $n$, by step 1, $\Gamma(u(V),\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^n})\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^n}(V)=(f_*\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^n})_V\circ(\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^n})_V=(f_*\varepsilon_{\mathcal I^n}\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal I^n})_V=\mathrm{id}$, by the triangle identity $f_*\varepsilon\circ\eta_{f_*}=\mathrm{id}_{f_*}$ of the adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3). So the chain map of step 5 is the identity of the complex $\Gamma(V,f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal I^\bullet)$, and by steps 4 and 5 $e^p_{V,\mathcal F}=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}\circ\iota^p_{f_*\mathcal I}$, a composite of two isomorphisms $H^p(V,f_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(\Gamma(V,f_*\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^p(\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal I^\bullet))\to H^p(u(V),\mathcal F)$. Hence $e^p_{V,\mathcal F}$ is an isomorphism for every $p\ge0$. In degree $0$, $f^*=\eta_{f_*\mathcal F}(V)$ ([lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] (1)) and $H^0(u(V),\varepsilon_{\mathcal F})=\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}(u(V))$ under $H^0=\Gamma$ ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2)), so $e^0=\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}(u(V))\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal F}(V)=(f_*\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}\circ\eta_{f_*\mathcal F})_V=\mathrm{id}$, the parenthetical remark of the statement.
